With vaccinations progressing and policy support still strong, activity and employment continue to firm, and the FOMC is tapering asset purchases while keeping the policy rate at 0–0.25 percent. The SLOOS points to broadly improving credit supply: banks eased standards across residential real estate (including HELOCs and jumbo), multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential CRE, and consumer credit; they also increased credit limits on cards and reduced auto loan rates. Foreign banks eased CRE standards and reported stronger CRE demand. Demand indicators are mixed—banks expect stronger demand for credit cards and C&I, and report stronger consumer loan demand, but some reported weaker current demand for C&I and auto—suggesting momentum but not uniformly strong. These SLOOS findings support accommodative financial conditions and credit intermediation, partially offsetting risks highlighted in the Financial Stability Report (stretched valuations, market fragilities, nonbank leverage, and pandemic‑sensitive CRE pressures) and elevated inflation. Netting these, the outlook remains cautiously optimistic, with a modestly more positive tilt given improved credit availability.
